note: Views field formatter provides one field formatter plugin (id views_field_formatter, label 'View') available on almost all field types. It renders a chosen View (stored as 'viewid::display') via a #type=>view render element, passing the field's value/entity as contextual arguments. Settings (schema field.formatter.settings.views_field_formatter): view (string), arguments (map of {checked,weight}), hide_empty (bool), multiple (bool), implode_character (string). No configure route, permission, Drush, or extra plugins. State lives on core.entity_view_display.<entity>.<bundle>.<mode> -> content.<field>.{type,settings}. Medium cases read back which view a field uses and its multiple/implode settings; hard cases switch a field to the View formatter (frontpage view) and enable multiple mode with an implode character, verified against the live view display. All fields namespaced field_vff_*; the referenced view (frontpage) already exists on the site.

evals.prompt: The Drupal 'Views field formatter' module lets a field be displayed using the result of a View. What is the field formatter's plugin id and its label, and roughly which field types can use it?
evals.expected_output: The formatter plugin id is views_field_formatter (label 'View'). It is available on almost all field types (string, entity_reference, list_*, number, date, link, image, file, text, uri, boolean, etc.).

evals.prompt: In the Views field formatter, how is the chosen View recorded in the formatter settings, and which setting makes a multi-value field render the view once per value?
evals.expected_output: The 'view' setting stores the view and display as a single string 'viewid::display' (e.g. frontpage::page_1). The 'multiple' boolean makes a multi-value field render the view once per value; 'implode_character' then joins the outputs. Other settings: arguments and hide_empty.

evals.prompt: How does the Views field formatter pass the field's data to the selected View so the view can react to it?
evals.expected_output: It embeds the view with a #type => 'view' render element and passes the field's value(s) and the host entity id as the view's contextual arguments; you choose which arguments are sent and their order via the 'arguments' setting.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article field field_vff_known is displayed using the Views field formatter ('View'). Inspect the live default view display for Article and state which view (and display) that field is configured to render.
evals.expected_output: field_vff_known uses views_field_formatter with settings.view = 'frontpage::page_1' (the frontpage view, page_1 display).

evals.prompt: On this site the multi-value Article field field_vff_multi uses the Views field formatter. Inspect the live view-display configuration and state whether 'multiple' (render once per value) is enabled and what implode character is set.
evals.expected_output: For field_vff_multi the views_field_formatter settings have multiple: true and implode_character: ', '.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a field field_vff_task on the default display. Using the Views field formatter module, change that field's formatter to 'View' so it renders the 'frontpage' view instead of the field's own value. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_vff_task component has type: views_field_formatter and settings.view starting with 'frontpage' (e.g. frontpage::page_1).

evals.prompt: On this site the multi-value Article field field_vff_mult already uses the Views field formatter. Configure it so the view is rendered once per field value (multiple mode) and the per-value outputs are joined with the string ' | ' (space pipe space). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: For field_vff_mult the views_field_formatter settings have multiple: true and implode_character: ' | '.
